birth.place: Oysterponds (Orient), Southold, Suffolk County, New York, USA

summary: John's 8th-great-grandfather; a Southold-born Tuthill who settled in Brookhaven and moved to the Orange County highlands in the 1740s.
bio:
Born about 1692 at Oysterponds, son of John Tuthill Jr. & Mehitable Wells (Alva Tuttle p. 279; Akerly 1898). Married Rachel Browne about 1714. Bought land in Brookhaven in 1714 and 1721; rated there in 1741 but not in 1749; moved to Ulster/Orange between 1742 and 1748; died about 1772. Akerly names his children as Daniel (will dated Goshen 1761), James and Benjamin 'and perhaps others' — not John, which is why John's link stays probable. His brother Freegift Tuthill (1698–1765) also moved from Brookhaven to New Windsor and Goshen; his brother John (III) of Southold, will 9 Jun 1740 (NY Wills III, Liber 15, pp. 400–1), left Brookhaven land to 'my brother James Tuthill' and named 'my brother Joseph Brown'. His son James Jr. of New Windsor, Ulster Co. (will 17 Mar 1756, Liber 20 p. 25) died young leaving five children and made 'my father, James Tuthill, and Selah Strong, both of Orange County, executors' — proving James Sr. moved to Orange County. Son Daniel of Goshen (will 1761, Liber 23 p. 130) named Joshua Brown executor, asked for burial 'decent without Pomp or State', witnesses John Brewster, Samuel Smith and Selah Strong. TREE CONFLICT: the Ancestry tree shows 'James M Tuthill 1692–1772' married to 'HANNAH S REEVE 1699–1764' (with gravestone photo). Research shows the tree merged two marriages of two brothers: Joshua Tuthill married Hannah Reeve; James married Rachel Browne (McCurdy p14551). Because James and Joshua were full brothers (both sons of Mehitable Wells), the Tuthill, King and Wells relationships survive either way; only the Reeve and Satterly ancestors are at risk. Preferred: James Tuthill & Rachel Browne (Round 2/3 research; uploads override tree).

The printed Brookhaven town records add detail to James's Long Island years. On 1 May 1721 land was laid out to him on the other half of Dayton's Right, next to his Chestnut Pound land and his 'former 50 lot'. This is the Dayton's Right land his brother John (d. 1743) also referred to ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]). In June 1737 he owned the westernmost 15-acre lot in Fireplace Neck 'at South', and a new highway was laid along the north ends of those lots at his request and his neighbours' ([R4-S1]). A 'James Tuttle, junr.' signs a town paper c.1738/9. On Alva Tuttle's list he is the son James b. 1717, later of New Windsor (d. 1756) ([R4-S1], [R4-S4]). In October 1741 James sat as one of four arbitrators in a town dispute ([R4-S1]). Fireplace Neck lies a few miles west of Moriches, the home of James Smith and Jerusha Topping, whose daughter Temperance married James's son John in 1752.

The tree gives James's wife as 'Hannah S. Reeve (1699-1764)'. Akerly (1898) shows that Hannah, daughter of Maj. James Reeve of Mattituck (d. 8 Mar 1764, aged 64), was the wife of James's brother **Joshua** Tuthill of Cutchogue ([R4-S2]). The tree has transferred Joshua's wife and her gravestone to James. James's wife was Rachel Browne (Alva Tuttle p. 279, via [R4-S4]).
